goal: Sleep anxiety I'm not sure if this belongs here, I can remove it if so, but it's 3 am and Im all alone and covered in sweat. I was kind of paralyzed in my bed for the past. Hour? Couple minutes? God knows how long. It was probably the most terrifying thing ever. I was sleeping but I was also aware. It was like my mind was tricking me over and over again into thinking I could wake up from this weird state of consciousness but I couldn't. Like being trapped just beneath the surface of water. It was the weirdest thing but not scary in itself. It only ever happened to me once before months ago but this was much, much much worse than that time. I kept trying to wake myself up again and again because I knew I was dreaming, but every time I got close to the surface of consciousness I was pulled back under. Like my mind was repeatedly trapping itself. First I was tossing and turning so badly (in my nightmare? ) trying to wake up because I knew something was wrong. I kept falling out of bed and I would "wake up" only to have the process repeat. Each successive time it got worse and worse. I can't really describe it. I was "falling" into sleep. I would jerk awake only to realize I was still in my dream and *that* was my nightmare. Last time this happened I was able to break the cycle much much sooner. This felt like it would never end. I know it's bizarre and it doesn't even sound scary but it's like being stuck in a scary part of your mind that doesn't want you to leave. It's more terrifying than any nightmare I've ever had. My question is, has this ever happened to anyone before? How do you stop it? The last time was months ago. This time seemed to last much longer. I don't want it to happen every again. Scared to go back to my bed now ;(

goal: This is crippling my life. Just need to vent somewhere - I’m 26, have been diagnosed with depression and anxiety since I was about 18 and I seem to work in cycles. A few months I’m on top of the world, excelling in whatever job I’m in, generally finding all relationships easier and feeling genuinely happy. Then, it turns. I fall apart mentally and self sabotage everything until I’ve alienated myself and I’m stuck, alone, in a room for days or weeks on end. I’m on heavy medication but that doesn’t seem to make much of a difference. This last year has possibly been the worst. I’ve always had a temper and been aggressive but lately I’ve been losing it to a point of physically harming others. I live with my cousin (male) and one of my best friends (female) and things have gotten so bad at certain points that I’ve physically assaulted both of them and feel disgusting for that. Currently I have no drive or motivation to do anything at all and can’t seem to get out of this “funk” this time. My room mates “try” to help but seem to make everything worse. I’m back on the path of feeling like suicide is the best option and I don’t want to feel this way. I want to feel like I deserve to have good things happen but every time I spin it and good things come around I feel like I don’t deserve it and throw it all away. Right now I barely eat, I only sleep through the day and it’s arguably my favourite time because it’s an escape.

goal: I FEEL LIKE SHIT RIGHT NOW. I FEEL LIKE SHIT RIGHT NOW. I don't know what to do. Or well I have several thoughts that are going through my head. Several that are extremely illogical and point blank stupid. Of those are essentially ways I imagine to end my life. I can hang myself or I can overdose. But I know all of these “scenarios” are stupid. So why can't I just shake it? Why do I just keep on thinking about it? Do I secretly think that maybe some part of it IS logical? But let's start by explaining what is the thing that triggered these emotions. It's stupid I know, but it's work. I know that the end all and be all of a person is not defined by the person's profession. However, you can't deny the fact that the persons profession is a large part of that individual's life. In short, I have been an utter failure at work when my depression hit and I am struggling to keep up. But the simple thoughts of. I need to get work done. I need to get my reports done. I need to get my visits scheduled. Thinking about these things sends several cyclical and debilitating emotions through my head. Thoughts of hopelessness, despair, impossible, monumental, and above all else that I struggle with the most is lack of ethical meaning. I know there are different schools of thoughts on how I can proceed - of the most prevalent is to come to the realization and accept the fact that I'm in the situation I am in and also the associated emotions with it. I need to take these emotions and understand that these are purely my thoughts/feelings and not necessarily reality. For however much it perceive it is reality - it is NOT. This is an important realization that I must differentiate. Thoughts are not reality. Emotions are not reality. Reality is reality and there is nothing in this world you can do about it. I needed to ground myself. I needed to write this out. I needed this as a distraction. I needed this to refocus. Thank you for listening.

In short, I have been an utter failure at work when my depression hit and I am struggling to keep up.
But the simple thoughts of.
I need to get work done.
I need to get my reports done.
I need to get my visits scheduled.
Thinking about these things sends several cyclical and debilitating emotions through my head.
Thoughts of hopelessness, despair, impossible, monumental, and above all else that I struggle with the most is lack of ethical meaning.

I know there are different schools of thoughts on how I can proceed - of the most prevalent is to come to the realization and accept the fact that I'm in the situation I am in and also the associated emotions with it.
I need to take these emotions and understand that these are purely my thoughts/feelings and not necessarily reality.
For however much it perceive it is reality - it is NOT.
This is an important realization that I must differentiate.
Thoughts are not reality.
Emotions are not reality.
Reality is reality and there is nothing in this world you can do about it.
I needed to ground myself.
I needed to write this out.
I needed this as a distraction.
I needed this to refocus.
Thank you for listening.

goal: I'm thirty-four and everything just keeps getting worse I heard a comedian make a joke about suicide once. The general gist of it was if you go to the movies and the first half is unrelenting shit then yeah, you can reasonably guess it's not going to get better and you may as well check out. I think it's finally really time to accept the reality that's been beating me over the head for as long as I can remember. Every moment I've not done it was fueled by denial. It's not going to get better. I've hoped it would for over 3 decades and it's about time I accept reality.

goal: I feel so alone. All the time. The suicidal thoughts are not the worst part of the situation I’ve been in for the last eight years. Nor is the Crohn’s disease. Or the anxiety. Or even the depression in general. It is the all-encompassing, soul-crushing loneliness that I feel all the time, every single day, that makes it all unbearable. I just want to be loved. To be listened to. Cared for. I just want someone to give me a hug. To tell me I matter and mean it. And yet, even if I get those things (which is rare), it’s not enough. It’s never enough. My twisted mind always finds some way to doubt it. Maybe they aren’t genuine. Maybe they’re just saying that. Why would a person as miserable and useless as me matter in the slightest to anyone other than perhaps my parents? And I know I’m not alone. I know hundreds of thousands of people, probably more, feel the exact same way I do. I know I have a family who cares about me. I know I have “friends,” even though I’m not close enough to any of them to talk about this stuff with. I know I have coworkers, and acquaintances, and friendly encounters, and social outings. But even surrounded by people, surrounded by proof of the contrary. I am always alone. If I could cry right now, I would. Instead I’ll just have to let the deafening silence lull me to sleep, only to experience the same misery all over again tomorrow. And the next day. And the day after that. After those three days though, I’m sure I’ll be fine. It’ll definitely pass. /s

goal: how do I deal with the realisation that anxiety is preventing me from succeeding in things that really, really matter? I had an exam about a month back and got the results back today. In preparation I studied for hours daily, struggling through my anxiety, brain fog, exhaustion, and whatnot. I am currently in a place where I sleep most of the day and still struggle to even leave the house. My parents are divorcing, my grandparents gravely ill, and I am seeing a doctor soon to get some sort of answer as to why my body is breaking down the way it is. Getting to lectures and lessons is a tremendous challenge. Despite this I felt like I truly aced the test; I had prepared, delivered, and left feeling confident I had written one of my best exams ever. or so I thought. Turns out I passed, but only just, and we don't get to retake tests. Meanwhile, my study buddies who had used the exact same notes and put in the exact same hours studying all got A's. As they all high fived each other in the classroom, I tried my best to hold back the tears at the realisation that whatever it was they had succeeded in doing, I had not. How do I deal with the fact that my anxiety is not only making the small things in life difficult, but also ruining my future chances at jobs, grades and scholarships? It feels beyond unfair that this undefeatable monster inside my head gets to decide everything for me. I pray to whatever deities may listen that I can somehow muster the strength to reach the potential I know I have within me.

goal: I feel like I'm the only adult in my life As the title states, I feel like I'm the only adult in my life. I'll try my best not to rant here. At work, I'm constantly having to address issues with employees not taking care of property or making preventable mistakes. I get in arguments with my boss on almost a daily basis because he doesn't listen to anyone and takes actions based on what he interprets. When I get home, I have the exact same problems. My wife is always upset at me because she thinks I'm always pointing out her mistakes instead of ignoring them. The thing is, I do ignore a lot of things but there's some things I can't ignore. Leaving a dirty diaper sitting out or going out and not locking the door are big things to me that I feel should be addressed. There are some small things (I'l admit they are minor) that I bring up because they are repeated annoyances, like leaving the bathroom door wide open where it blocks two other doors. There's so many more areas that I can discuss like this and I can see where my wife feels like I'm always pointing out problems, but in my mind I get upset that I bring something up the first time and it keeps happening over and over with complete disregard that it bothers me and occupies my mind. With all that being said, it's gone on at work and at home for so long that I feel like my mental health is going down the drain fast. I've dealt with depression before where I felt suicidal and I know that I'm headed into that dark place again. I just want someone in my life to step up as I have to help me carry this load of being a mature adult. Someone that listens when I say we have a problem and actually makes an effort to correct the problem. Someone to recognize how hard it is for me to be the only one that cares about the details that impact the big picture. Someone to think for themselves and have pride in something. I don't know if I'm asking too much or not enough. The only thing I know right now is how it's affecting me and it isn't good. Thank you for reading and sorry I made this post so long.

goal: Just a little note about mine today. Sometimes it feels like every muscle in my body is flexing all at once. Like every fiber of my being is being stretched so thin the threads will tear and I'll spontaneously combust. Other times I can't feel my limbs. My brain is so focused on my rapid heartbeat and every fucked up thought in my head that the rest of me just doesn't exist. My arms lay motionless and heavy against my pillow, but they aren't cold or itchy, there's no pain because it's all in my head and my chest where my heart raps it's unsteady beat against my ribcage begging for my head to just stop thinking about why he wore that with her but not with me, or why people that barely know me seem to hate me. They probably don't, but in my head they're always talking about how horrible I am for just existing. Then my stomach chimes in with a heavy drop and my fingers tap out these words on a screen that seems so foreign to me. "I didn't mean that thing I said," but I did, at least, anxious me did. I spewed those words pointedly, hoping to evoke a response. and it worked. For a moment in time anxiety won her little battle while I wept inside for the girl that knows better than to let her win.

goal: Anxious associations I've been dealing with anxiety since I was young and have recently realized a pattern about my anxiety. Certain places I've felt anxious at in the past I will start to associate with those feelings, and subsequently those places will start to cause anxiety in themselves. This has recently started with my new workplace. I enjoy (well, enjoyed) my job and it is in a field I am passionate about. However, my anxiety has increased lately and I am now associating these feelings with work and the workplace itself. I have left work early twice now because the feelings get severe enough that I feel sick. This compounds things because I then worry that I'm not a good employee and why can't I just be ok at a job I like. Does anyone have any tips about how to not associate anxiety and panic with unrelated things? Thank you!

In counseling, I hope to explore evidence-based techniques such as cognitive-behavioral therapy or relaxation exercises to alleviate anxiety symptoms. It would be beneficial to discuss practical steps for managing stress and developing healthier coping mechanisms specific to my anxiety triggers.

goal: I lost everyone Hey I'm 15 yo boy and i always wanted to have someone who would genuinely care for me. I've always been shy and bad at making friends. Idk the source of my shyness, maybe it's because my dad left me when I was 2 and I always waited for him to come back? I felt that I was worse than everybody, because I didn't have dad, I couldn't ride a bike, I was fat, I was bad at sports (these all things didn't change at all since then). I cried a lot because my grandma often screamed at me because I did something wrong ( I was just a child). Everyone in the family didn't cared too much about me crying ( they cared but I never heard "sorry"). Through preschool and middle school I had few friends but most of them were toxic to me but I couldn't stand up to them. In 4th grade I had a crush on this one girl ( I still do) but she doesn't like me back. In 7th grade I met my group of friends that I would hang out with but I still felt kinda left behind. I was very positive about going to high school because of the new people. Nobody talked to me though. It felt surreal to not have anyone to hang out with or don't say a word for a whole day. I changed school to previous one where I had 1 friend. It felt awesome to have a friend. After 2 months he was a stranger to me. Now my grades are much worse than before, because I just don't have motivation. All my friends and family members from my life are gone. They just fade away. I don't have a close relationship with anyone in my family. Everyone (teachers, classmates, family) thinks I'm antisocial and isolating myself on purpose. I feel like disappointment because I'm not trying enough to be better and have better grades or be better at sports or be more social. I just wanna make someone proud of me. For most of this year I felt numb or horny. I kept pushing forward. I never thought of cuting myself it was so ridiculous to me. But one day I just felt so ugly and classmates invited me to hang out with them but I felt useless and I was just there and I just couldn't interact with them because I fucking lost my identity and I felt that they hate me because of this and I was so overwhelmed by the thought that I can't be social and that everyone thinks that I'm so weird and ugly so I cut myself and it felt good. Now I started to feel sad again because of all the friends that i don't have in my life anymore and that no one cares about my feelings and expects me to be someone that I'm not. I don't know who I am. I don't know how to make friends. I want to feel that I exist. I just want to have friends, girlfriend and good relationship with family, but I know I just can't open to anyone. It makes me angry that I can't express myself and that I can't live a life I want. The urge to cut myself is bigger and bigger and I'm doing it more frequently now. I have hope that someone understands me and that I'll be happy but this hope fades  and more scars show up on my body.

goal: I stumbled upon this sub down a reddit wormhole And I wanted to reach out to you all. It happens to be the birthday of a close friend of mine who killed herself just over a year ago. No one close to her understood/knew at all what she was going through or how she was feeling. We must have been pretty shitty support to her. But god, I wish we'd known, so we could have been there. A few years ago I felt super down. I was never realistically going to end my life, but I thought about it every day, and would do little things like not wear seatbelts to make it more likely that I'd die in a random scenario. Maybe that seems a bit naive if you've been feeling like this for a long time. But please don't give up on yourself. You're not giving up on eachother when you offer supportive advice. Please extend yourself the same courtesy.

goal: My mom told me to kill myself I want to start off by saying that i'm 22, I grew up in an abusive home, physically and emotionally, which is probably why I ended up the way I did. My dad's no longer physically abusive, although sometimes emotionally he is. I've dealt with depression for about a decade now. Since this started, my life has continuously gone downhill, worse, and worse. I used to self harm, I've had many suicide attempts but my most serious one was when I slit my neck with a scalpel (I know how crazy it sounds I don't like talking about it because people think I'm insane probably), my family was devastated, it was the first time I saw my dad break down while they were all in the hospital. My mom was in shock. When I got home afterwards, they were so careful with me. Always tried to make me happy. Always scared I was going to do it again. After my suicide attempt, I started using heroin to cope with my depression, and it worked, really well. Until I overdosed, and after eventually destroyed my life because of it. The point is, my family knows how serious my struggles are. They've almost lost me 3 times now. When I sleep, my parents sometimes come to check on me to see if i'm still breathing. That's how scared they are of losing me. They're always on edge, my whole family is, including my siblings, they're all always on edge that i'm going to kill myself. And I probably will. goal: It’s 3am I feel super sick - here’s my story, just in case it’s the only place I get to tell it When I was younger I wanted to be a writer; I had this vision that I could write for somewhere like the New York Times and release a few books along the way. When I was younger I still wrote for fun, my grammar was sloppier and more haphazard, but I had all these colours to choose from. My writing then was saturated. Now, I don’t write unless I have to. My writing is technically better, but all I have are shades of beige; I constantly feel like I’m writing for someone else and subsequently everything feels just slightly inauthentic. Calculated, not colourful. In a way it’s a good metaphor for where I am now, all the colour I thought adult life would bring me has gone. In reality I know when I was younger my sadness was just more repressed; that I wasn’t ever really happy - but, I had better moments. It may have been denial, but I’d kill to believe I wasn’t depressed again. If you didn’t get it already, I’m much older now and somehow despite more therapy and much more effort, I’m also much sadder. I have these two mindsets around death. The first, I’m sure drawn from literature, paints death in this kind of (problematically) endearing way - I picture killing myself as drowning at the beach I’d go to with my dad as a kid. I imagine the colour lifting from my skin under the water, like it was paint and my body a canvas. In death I envision this idea of absolution; that everything has had a purpose leading up to now, and all the sadness and all the pain can finally be let go of. The other picture I have of suicide is the more realistic, it’s me writing letters to all my loved ones, dying alone in a hotel room (sparing details here for obvious reasons). The latter is meaningless and all it represents is the passing of all the pain I have being dispersed amongst the people I love most. My life now content wise is good I guess, I have a boyfriend who I love more than anything in the world, and beautiful deeply caring thoughtful friends. I’ll graduate a lawyer from a top tier university in a few years (assuming I’m still here). I have pretty much everything that I thought would make me happy. It’s just never enough. I always think when I sit down to write a post here, which I usually delete after 2 minutes, that I’ll chronicle all that has gone wrong in my life. A history of abuse and misfortune that lead to now. But my life is so adversely different to when I was a child that all of the trauma I have now feels so abstract; it basically feels like all this stuff happened to someone else but I’m the one who ended up feeling it. I got my wisdom teeth removed yesterday or the day before; you might have seen a two second post that I put up and then thought better of. I know that I’ll be better in a few days, but I’ve been so suicidal this month that having anything go wrong just feels like a death sentence. I’m running on absolute empty and whilst the intellectual part of my brain knows that I will probably start functioning again, right now I just want it all to stop. I don’t even have the energy to make this a proper letter (in the ultimate irony I’ve not killed myself many times because I haven’t found the energy to write letters first). I don’t know what I want out of writing this, I think my sadness just feels so disconnected that I hope turning it into something will give it meaning. I’m just so tired of trying, I feel like I’m fighting to stay alive everyday but I also don’t want to be alive; and this paradox is slowly killing me. The next few days will be bad for me, I struggle to stay alive when I have no reasons to want to die, but this current pain and sickness is giving me a legitimacy I don’t usually have. I’m always shocked to learn I have a no lowest point. If you’ve read this far, wish me luck I guess? Sorry this wasn’t really anything substantive, apparently I don’t have that in me tonight.

About 5 months ago, I moved out of my abusive household. I did it, I got out, but then the dorms ate up my savings and I was having a bit of a crisis; I now had 5 months to plan where I’ll go after this, no car, no credit, fully independent from my parents with no clue how to do shit because I’ve essentially been a captive for 7 years who had to learn everything about the world completely on my own. So now we’re here. I have some rigorous classes, so I’ve been focusing on those, I’ve been trying to work of Fiverr to have a little bit of income, I’ve been bringing myself out of constant depressive and suicidal episodes by reminding myself I actually have a life goal to look forward to now and everything was getting a little better really slowly. I have nowhere to go, I don’t have a job, most people don’t have a job right now because everyone’s work is getting shut down. No one can afford to take anyone in right now even if I did feel like I had a friend I could stay with, and I can imagine trying to get an apartment right now with everything going on is probably impossible even for someone with good credit and a job. Nothing is looking good right now. There’s no more hope for me in my opinion. If I don’t commit now, there’s no way I’m coming out of this virus thing not on the street or in some sort of forced housing situation. I’ve made the decision to stop doing my schoolwork altogether and spend the rest of the break enjoying it as much as possible before I kms.

goal: I have to say, Alex, that addiction has been such a painful journey for me. The struggle to overcome it has been overwhelming. But I'm here, seeking therapy, which I see as a step towards success. Success, for me, would be reclaiming control over my life. Breaking free from the chains of addiction and rediscovering the joy and purpose that I once had. It's about rebuilding relationships, finding peace within myself, and living a healthier, more fulfilling life. Well, it started with peer pressure in my teenage years. I wanted to fit in, feel accepted. Alcohol seemed like a way to escape my insecurities and have fun. Gradually, it became a crutch to numb the pain I felt inside. I guess I didn't realize it would lead to this painful cycle of addiction. Addiction has devastated my relationships, Alex. I've hurt the people I love the most, pushing them away in my pursuit of the substance. It's caused so much pain and mistrust, and I'm left feeling isolated and ashamed. My daily life has revolved around getting my fix, sacrificing my responsibilities and passions along the way. I reached a point where the pain of addiction outweighed the temporary relief it provided. I saw my life spiraling out of control, and I couldn't keep pretending that everything was fine. I realized that seeking help was a crucial step towards reclaiming my life and finding lasting success. One of the biggest challenges I foresee is breaking free from the familiar patterns and routines associated with addiction. It's difficult to imagine a life without relying on substances for comfort and escape. I also worry about managing cravings and preventing relapse when faced with triggers in my environment. Thank you, Alex. Your words give me hope and comfort in this challenging process. I understand that it will take time and dedication, but I am committed to making the necessary changes. The pain of addiction won't define me; success in recovery will.

goal: I'm feeling so lonely lately, especially since my girlfriend left me. Well, we were together for a few years, but things started falling apart. I guess I let my anxiety get the best of me. I was always worried about what she was doing, who she was talking to. It was suffocating for both of us. I constantly questioned her, doubted her loyalty, and felt insecure whenever she spent time with others. It put a strain on our relationship, and eventually, she couldn't handle it anymore. I've thought about it, but I feel so discouraged right now. I can't help but think that my anxiety will ruin any future relationships too. Maybe it's just better if I stay alone. I guess I'm just scared of repeating the same patterns. I don't want to hurt someone else because of my anxiety. I've thought about it, but I'm not sure if it would really help. I've tried different things in the past, but nothing seems to make a lasting difference. I suppose it couldn't hurt to give it another shot. But what if I never find someone who can understand and accept me with all my anxiety? I really want to believe that, but my past experiences have left me feeling doubtful. It's like my anxiety keeps pushing people away. I guess I just need to have faith that there's someone out there who will be patient and understanding. It's just hard to see it right now. Thank you, Alex. I know it won't be easy, but talking to you has given me a glimmer of hope. I'll do my best to work on myself and not let my anxiety control my life.

goal: I'm surprised, Alex. I never thought I'd find myself in therapy, but the truth is, I need help. I've been struggling with addiction, and it's been taking control of my life. The bullying voice in my head keeps telling me I'm weak and that I'll never overcome this. It's constantly telling me that I'm not strong enough to break free from addiction. It says that I'm a failure, unworthy of love and happiness. It makes me doubt myself and my ability to change. I think the voice became more prominent when I started using substances as a way to cope with stress and painful experiences. It was like a vicious cycle, where the more I used, the louder and stronger the voice became. I never realized how deeply it affected my self-esteem until now. Well, now that I think about it, there was a time in my childhood when I went through a lot of changes and stress. My parents divorced, and I had to move to a new town, leaving behind my friends and everything familiar. It was a difficult time, and I felt lonely and lost. I guess that's when I started seeking solace in substances. I believe that understanding the root causes of my addiction will help me gain clarity and find healthier ways to cope. By acknowledging and processing those past traumas, I can learn to heal myself from within. It's like untangling a knot, one loop at a time. Actually, I have. I've reached out to a few close friends and my sister, who have been incredibly supportive. They've shared their addiction recovery stories with me, and it's reassuring to know I'm not alone in this battle. I've always loved hiking and being in nature. It brings me peace and allows me to disconnect from stress and negative thoughts. I've also started journaling, which helps me process my emotions and reflect on my recovery journey. I've realized that it's important to prioritize self-care and make intentional choices. By setting aside dedicated time for hiking and journaling, I can create a routine that supports my well-being. It's about making myself a priority and committing to my own healing. Thank you, Alex. I'm really grateful for your guidance and support. This conversation has already given me so much clarity and hope. I'm excited to continue working towards a life free from addiction and filled with joy and self-love.
